Used for display in SAP, Teamcenter PLM, and reporting tools.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – BOM Header Description; Siemens Teamcenter PLM

description: The maximum depth/level of the BOM hierarchy for this manufacturing BOM (e.g., 1 = single-level, 5 = five levels deep). Used to understand BOM complexity and to control multi-level BOM explosion in MRP and production scheduling.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – Multi-Level BOM; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Current lifecycle state of the manufacturing BOM. 'draft' indicates the BOM is under engineering review. 'released' means it has been authorized for production use. 'frozen' indicates no further changes are permitted (e.g., during active production run). 'superseded' means a newer BOM version has replaced it. 'obsolete' means the BOM is no longer valid.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module – BOM Status; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1; Siemens Teamcenter PLM BOM Management

description: Classification of the BOM by its intended use in the manufacturing process. 'production' is the standard mBOM used on the shop floor. 'phantom' represents sub-assemblies that are not stocked. 'sales' is used for variant configuration. 'spare_parts' is for after-sales service. 'co_product' is for by-products in manufacturing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Module – BOM Category; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: SAP BOM usage indicator defining the organizational context in which the BOM is applied. 'production' (SAP usage 1) is the standard for shop floor manufacturing. 'engineering' (SAP usage 2) is for design/development. 'universal' (SAP usage 3) applies across all usages. Determines which BOM is selected during MRP and production order processing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – BOM Usage (T415); IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Version identifier of the manufacturing BOM (e.g., 'v1.0', 'v2.3'). Incremented each time the BOM is revised through an approved Engineering Change Order. Enables version history tracking and rollback capability for quality investigations.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM – BOM Versioning; IATF 16949 Clause 7.5; SAP PP BOM Change History

description: Free-text description of the business reason for creating or modifying this BOM version (e.g., 'Cost reduction – substitute supplier for part X', 'Regulatory compliance – CARB Tier 3 emission update', 'Quality improvement – NVH fix per TSB-2024-001'). Required for IATF 16949 change control documentation.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.6 – Control of Changes; SAP PP Change Master; ISO 9001 Clause 8.5.6

description: Total number of distinct component line items (BOM positions) in this manufacturing BOM. Provides a quick indicator of BOM complexity and is used for completeness validation during BOM release. Does not include phantom sub-assembly components.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – BOM Item Count; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Timestamp when this manufacturing BOM record was first created in the source system (SAP PP or Teamcenter PLM). Represents the business event of BOM creation, not the ETL load time. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per enterprise data standards.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 7.5 – Documented Information; ISO 9001 Clause 7.5; SAP PP BOM Header

description: The Engineering Change Order (ECO) number that authorized the creation or last modification of this manufacturing BOM. Provides full traceability from the shop floor BOM back to the formal engineering change management process in Teamcenter PLM. Required for IATF 16949 change control compliance.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM – Engineering Change Management; IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.6; SAP PP ECO Integration

description: The date after which this manufacturing BOM version is no longer valid for production use. Corresponds to the SAP BOM 'Valid To' date. Null indicates the BOM is open-ended with no planned expiry. Used to manage BOM transitions during model year changeovers and End of Production (EOP).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – BOM Effectivity; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: The date from which this manufacturing BOM version becomes effective and valid for production use. Corresponds to the SAP BOM 'Valid From' date. Used for date-effective BOM explosion in MRP and production order creation. Aligns with Start of Production (SOP) planning.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – BOM Effectivity; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1; SAE J1739

description: The planned or actual End of Production (EOP) date for the vehicle program associated with this BOM. Marks the milestone when serial production of this vehicle configuration ceases. Used for last-time-buy planning, spare parts provisioning, and regulatory compliance archiving.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.1; SAP PP Production Planning; APQP

description: Status of the regulatory homologation (type approval) for the vehicle configuration defined by this BOM in the target regulatory market. 'approved' is required before vehicles built to this BOM can be legally sold in the target market. Managed through the Regulatory Compliance and Homologation process.
reference: NHTSA 49 CFR Part 567 – Certification; UNECE WP.29 Type Approval; Euro NCAP; DOT FMVSS

description: Indicates whether this BOM uses SAP Variant Configuration (VC) to support multiple vehicle variants from a single configurable BOM structure. True = configurable BOM with characteristic-based component selection. False = fixed BOM for a single specific vehicle configuration.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – Variant Configuration (LO-VC); IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Indicates whether the header material of this BOM is a phantom assembly — a logical grouping of components that is not physically stocked or produced as a discrete unit. Phantom assemblies are 'exploded through' during MRP and production order processing. Common for sub-assemblies in JIS manufacturing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – Phantom Assembly (Special Procurement Key 50); IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this manufacturing BOM record in the source system. Used to detect changes during incremental data loads into the Databricks Silver Layer and to support BOM change history auditing required by IATF 16949.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 7.5 – Documented Information; SAP PP BOM Change History; ISO 9001 Clause 7.5

description: SAP material number of the header material (finished vehicle or major assembly) for which this BOM is defined. This is the top-level material in the BOM hierarchy, corresponding to the vehicle configuration or assembly unit.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM – Material Master (MM60); SAP PP BOM Header

description: The four-digit automotive Model Year (MY) for which this manufacturing BOM is valid (e.g., 2025). Determines the applicable regulatory standards, feature content, and homologation requirements. Aligns with NHTSA and EPA model year definitions.
reference: NHTSA 49 CFR Part 565 – VIN; SAP PP Material Master; IATF 16949

description: SAP plant code identifying the specific manufacturing facility where this mBOM is used for production (e.g., 'P001' for Detroit Assembly, 'P002' for Osaka Plant). Determines plant-specific routing, work centers, and local regulatory compliance requirements.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP/MM – Plant Master; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1

description: Classification of the vehicle powertrain technology for which this BOM is defined. ICE = Internal Combustion Engine, HEV = Hybrid Electric Vehicle, PHEV = Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle, BEV = Battery Electric Vehicle, FCEV = Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle. Determines applicable emissions regulations (EPA, CARB, WLTP) and BOM component sets.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 86 – Emissions Standards; CARB Title 13; CAFE Standards; SAE J1711

description: Status of the Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) for the components in this BOM. PPAP is the AIAG/IATF 16949 process that verifies supplier components meet design and specification requirements before production launch. 'approved' is required before the BOM can be released to production.
reference: AIAG PPAP 4th Edition; IATF 16949 Clause 8.4.1; SAP QM – Quality Notifications

description: BOM number of the previous manufacturing BOM version that this BOM supersedes. Enables backward navigation in the BOM version chain for change impact analysis and quality investigations. Null for the initial BOM version.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – BOM Change History; IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.6; Siemens Teamcenter PLM

description: Code identifying the specific production line or assembly line within the plant for which this BOM is configured (e.g., 'LINE-A', 'TRIM-CHASSIS-1'). Used in Apriso/Dassault MES for shop floor routing and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) scheduling.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES – Shop Floor Execution; SAP PP Work Center; IATF 16949 Clause 8.5

description: Code identifying the target regulatory market for which this BOM is homologated (e.g., 'US-FEDERAL', 'US-CARB', 'EU-EURO6', 'JP-JC08', 'CN-CHINA6'). Determines applicable emissions standards (EPA, CARB, Euro 6, WLTP), safety regulations (NHTSA FMVSS, UNECE), and CAFE compliance requirements.
reference: NHTSA 49 CFR – FMVSS; EPA 40 CFR Part 86; CARB Title 13; Euro NCAP; UNECE WP.29; CAFE Standards

description: The date on which this manufacturing BOM was formally released to production (status changed to 'released'). Marks the point at which the BOM is authorized for use in production orders and MRP planning. Corresponds to the SAP BOM release date.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – BOM Release; IATF 16949 Clause 8.1; APQP Phase 4

description: User ID or employee identifier of the manufacturing engineer or release authority who formally released this BOM to production in SAP PP or Teamcenter PLM. Required for audit trail and change control compliance under IATF 16949.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 7.5 – Documented Information; SAP PP Authorization; ISO 9001 Clause 7.5

description: Alphanumeric revision level of the BOM (e.g., 'A', 'B', 'C' or '01', '02'). Used in conjunction with bom_version to track incremental changes within a version. Aligns with SAP BOM revision level and Teamcenter PLM revision management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – BOM Revision; Siemens Teamcenter PLM; IATF 16949 Clause 7.5

description: SAP routing number linking this manufacturing BOM to the associated production routing (sequence of operations, work centers, and standard times). The BOM and routing together define the complete manufacturing recipe for the vehicle. Corresponds to SAP PP routing header (CA01).
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – Routing (CA01/CA02); IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.1

description: The planned or actual Start of Production (SOP) date for the vehicle program associated with this BOM. Marks the milestone when serial production begins using this BOM configuration. Critical for program management, supplier readiness, and PPAP completion tracking.
reference: APQP Phase 4 – Product and Process Validation; IATF 16949 Clause 8.3; SAP PP Production Planning

description: BOM number of the newer manufacturing BOM that has replaced this one (populated when bom_status = 'superseded'). Enables forward navigation in the BOM version chain for traceability and historical analysis. Null when this is the current active BOM.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – BOM Change History; IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.6; Siemens Teamcenter PLM

description: Code identifying the specific vehicle configuration (variant) for which this BOM is defined, including body style, drivetrain, trim level, and market variant (e.g., 'SUV-AWD-PREMIUM-NA'). Used in SAP Variant Configuration (VC) to select the correct BOM components for a specific vehicle order.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP – Variant Configuration; Dassault ENOVIA Configuration Management; IATF 16949

description: Internal OEM code identifying the vehicle model (nameplate) for which this mBOM is defined (e.g., 'F150', 'RAV4', 'MODEL3'). Used to associate the BOM with the correct vehicle program in PLM and SAP.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM – Product Structure; SAP PP Material Master

description: Primary key for production_variant
Foreign key linking to compliance.homologation_record. Business justification: Variant definitions are approved via homologation; linking ensures variant builds only when approved.
Foreign key linking to vehicle.model. Business justification: Variant Definition Process links each variant to its vehicle model for configuration management and regulatory compliance.
Reference to the manufacturing plant where this production variant is authorized to be built. Determines line compatibility, tooling availability, and regulatory homologation scope.

Reference to the manufacturing BOM (Bill of Materials) version applicable to this production variant. Links to the BOM master in Siemens Teamcenter PLM or SAP MM (Materials Management) to resolve component lists for production planning and MRP (Material Requirements Planning) execution.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.3.5 — Design and Development Outputs; SAP MM BOM Management

description: Reference to the specific production line within the plant on which this variant is authorized to be assembled. Drives JIS (Just-in-Sequence) feasibility validation and takt time allocation.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.5 — Production and Service Provision

description: Reference to the manufacturing routing (operation sequence) applicable to this production variant in SAP PP (Production Planning). Defines the sequence of work centers, operations, and standard times required to build this variant from stamping through final assembly.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.1 — Control of Production; SAP PP Routing

description: Foreign key linking to engineering.vehicle_program. Business justification: Variants are defined under a vehicle program; variant management reports require vehicle_program_id.

business_glossary_term: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) Automation Level
description: SAE J3016 automation level of the ADAS (Advanced Driver Assistance Systems) suite fitted to this production variant: L0 (no automation), L1 (driver assistance), L2 (partial automation), L2_PLUS (enhanced partial automation), L3 (conditional automation). Drives ECU (Electronic Control Unit) software configuration, OTA (Over-the-Air Update) eligibility, and UNECE UN R157 regulatory compliance.
reference: SAE J3016 — Taxonomy of Driving Automation; UNECE UN R157 — ALKS; NHTSA AV Policy

description: Numeric score (1–10) representing the relative assembly complexity of this production variant compared to the base variant on the same production line. Higher scores indicate more assembly operations, longer cycle times, or specialized tooling requirements. Used for JIS (Just-in-Sequence) sequencing optimization to balance line loading and avoid consecutive high-complexity builds.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.1; SAE J4000 — Lean Manufacturing Assessment

description: Usable battery pack capacity in kilowatt-hours (kWh) for BEV, PHEV, and HEV variants. Null for pure ICE variants. Drives assembly sequencing for battery marriage station, WLTP (Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure) range certification, and EPA electric range labelling.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 600 — Fuel Economy; WLTP Regulation (EU) 2017/1151; SAE J1634

description: Standardized code identifying the vehicle body configuration for this production variant (e.g., SEDAN, SUV, TRUCK, COUPE, HATCHBACK, MINIVAN). Determines stamping die sets, body shop tooling, and paint booth configuration requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SEDAN|SUV|TRUCK|COUPE|HATCHBACK|MINIVAN|CONVERTIBLE|WAGON|VAN|CROSSOVER — promote to reference product]
reference: SAE J1100 — Vehicle Dimensions; ISO 3833 — Road Vehicles Types

description: Certified CO2 tailpipe emission in grams per kilometre (g/km) under WLTP or NEDC test cycle for this production variant. Used for EU CO2 fleet average compliance (Regulation (EU) 2019/631), CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) calculations, and vehicle taxation band classification in destination markets.
reference: EU Regulation 2019/631 — CO2 Standards for Cars; EPA 40 CFR Part 86; CARB Title 13

description: Timestamp when this production variant record was first created in the manufacturing master data system. Provides audit trail for data governance and IATF 16949 documented information control requirements.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 7.5 — Documented Information; ISO 9001 Clause 7.5

description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code identifying the primary market for which this production variant is homologated and destined (e.g., 'USA', 'DEU', 'JPN'). Governs regulatory compliance requirements (NHTSA FMVSS, Euro NCAP, UNECE), emission standards, and right-hand vs left-hand drive configuration.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; NHTSA FMVSS; UNECE Vehicle Regulations; Euro NCAP

description: Drivetrain configuration specifying which axles receive motive power: FWD (Front-Wheel Drive), RWD (Rear-Wheel Drive), AWD (All-Wheel Drive), or 4WD (Four-Wheel Drive). Determines chassis assembly routing, driveshaft fitment, and NVH (Noise Vibration Harshness) validation requirements.

Total engine displacement in cubic centimetres (cc) for ICE (Internal Combustion Engine) and HEV/PHEV variants. Null for BEV and FCEV variants. Used for regulatory classification under EPA, CARB, and UNECE emissions standards, and for CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) fleet averaging calculations.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 86; UNECE Regulation No. 83 — Emissions

description: Current engineering change revision level for this production variant as managed in Siemens Teamcenter PLM or PTC Windchill (e.g., 'A', 'B', 'C1', 'REV3'). Tracks design maturity and ensures the correct BOM (Bill of Materials) version is applied during production. Incremented upon each approved engineering change notice (ECN).
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.3.6 — Design and Development Changes; Siemens Teamcenter PLM ECM

description: Date on which this production variant is scheduled to cease production (EOP — End of Production). Drives last-order scheduling, tooling decommissioning planning, and spare parts provisioning for after-sales service obligations.
reference: APQP Phase 5 — Feedback, Assessment and Corrective Action; IATF 16949

description: EPA-certified combined fuel economy in miles per gallon (MPG) for ICE, HEV, and PHEV variants in NAFTA markets. Null for BEV/FCEV variants. Used for CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) fleet compliance reporting to EPA and consumer window sticker labelling under 49 CFR Part 575.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 600 — Fuel Economy; CAFE Standards 49 CFR Part 533; NHTSA

description: Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) in kilograms for this production variant. Used for regulatory classification under DOT FMVSS, UNECE weight regulations, and CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) fleet averaging. Also drives chassis assembly torque specifications and suspension tuning parameters.
reference: NHTSA FMVSS 120; UNECE Regulation No. 13 — Braking; DOT 49 CFR Part 571

description: Steering wheel position for this production variant: LHD (Left-Hand Drive) for markets such as USA, Germany; RHD (Right-Hand Drive) for markets such as UK, Japan, Australia. Determines instrument panel assembly variant, steering column routing, and body shop tooling configuration.
reference: UNECE Regulation No. 48 — Installation of Lighting; ISO 4130

description: Regulatory type-approval and homologation status for this production variant in the target destination market: PENDING (application submitted), CERTIFIED (full approval granted), CONDITIONAL (provisional approval with conditions), EXPIRED (certification lapsed), NOT_REQUIRED. Governs whether the variant can be legally sold in the destination market.
reference: UNECE WP.29 — Type Approval; NHTSA FMVSS Certification; Euro NCAP; DOT 49 CFR Part 567

description: Indicates whether this production variant can be produced as a CKD (Completely Knocked Down) kit for assembly at an overseas plant (True = CKD eligible). Drives export documentation, customs tariff classification, and overseas plant BOM (Bill of Materials) configuration in SAP MM.
reference: WTO Customs Valuation Agreement; SAP MM CKD Processing; IATF 16949

description: Indicates whether this production variant is eligible for JIS (Just-in-Sequence) supplier call-off sequencing (True = JIS eligible). JIS-eligible variants require sequenced component delivery synchronized to the build sequence, impacting supplier logistics contracts and MES call-off trigger configuration.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.4 — Control of Externally Provided Processes; SAE J4000

description: Indicates whether this production variant has been validated as feasible for assembly on the assigned production line (True = compatible, False = not compatible). Serves as the primary gate flag in MES (Manufacturing Execution System) build sequence feasibility validation and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) call-off authorization.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.1 — Control of Production; Apriso/Dassault MES

description: Indicates whether this production variant supports OTA (Over-the-Air) software updates for ECU (Electronic Control Unit) and infotainment systems (True = OTA capable). Drives connected vehicle service provisioning in Geotab/Bosch IoT platform and UNECE UN R156 software update regulatory compliance.
reference: UNECE UN R156 — Software Update Processes; NHTSA Cybersecurity Best Practices; SAE J3101

description: Maximum number of consecutive units of this production variant that can be scheduled back-to-back in the build sequence without violating line balancing or ergonomic constraints. Enforced by MES (Manufacturing Execution System) JIS (Just-in-Sequence) sequencing rules to prevent operator fatigue and tooling overload.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.1 — Control of Production; Apriso/Dassault MES Sequencing Rules

description: Cross-reference identifier for this production variant in the Apriso/Dassault MES (Manufacturing Execution System). Used for real-time build sequence call-off, WIP (Work in Progress) tracking, and quality gate routing on the shop floor.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES — Shop Floor Execution; IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.1

description: Four-digit model year (MY) for which this production variant is defined and authorized. Governs BOM (Bill of Materials) version applicability, regulatory homologation, and CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) compliance grouping. Range: 2000–2040.
reference: NHTSA 49 CFR Part 565 — VIN Requirements; EPA CAFE Standards

business_glossary_term: New Car Assessment Programme (NCAP) Safety Rating
description: Overall NCAP (New Car Assessment Programme) safety star rating achieved by this production variant (1 to 5 stars, or NOT_RATED if not yet assessed). Applicable to Euro NCAP, NHTSA NCAP, or ANCAP depending on destination market. Used for regulatory compliance reporting and marketing communications.
reference: Euro NCAP Assessment Protocol; NHTSA 5-Star Safety Ratings Program; ANCAP

description: Code identifying the bundled option package associated with this production variant (e.g., 'TECH_PKG', 'SAFETY_PKG', 'LUXURY_PKG'). Maps to a specific set of BOM (Bill of Materials) components and assembly operations in Siemens Teamcenter PLM and SAP PP configurable material management.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM — Variant Configuration; SAP PP — Configurable Materials (KMAT)

description: Classification of the paint application process required for this production variant: STANDARD (solid colour), METALLIC, PEARL, MATTE, or TWO_TONE. Determines paint booth routing, cure cycle parameters, and paint material BOM (Bill of Materials) components in the body shop and paint shop assembly stages.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.1 — Control of Production; ISO 12647 — Colour Standards

description: Classification of the vehicle powertrain technology for this variant: ICE (Internal Combustion Engine), HEV (Hybrid Electric Vehicle), PHEV (Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle), BEV (Battery Electric Vehicle), or FCEV (Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle). Drives assembly process routing, tooling requirements, and EPA/CARB emissions compliance classification.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 86 — Emissions Standards; CARB Title 13; SAE J1715

description: Current PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) approval status for this production variant. PPAP approval is a mandatory quality gate before SOP (Start of Production) under IATF 16949. Status values: NOT_REQUIRED, PENDING, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED. Drives production release authorization in MES.
reference: AIAG PPAP 4th Edition; IATF 16949 Clause 8.3.4 — Design and Development Controls

description: Regulatory compliance region grouping for this production variant, used to apply the correct homologation ruleset: NAFTA (North America), EU (European Union), APAC (Asia-Pacific), LATAM (Latin America), MEA (Middle East & Africa), CHINA. Determines applicable NCAP (New Car Assessment Programme) standards, emissions regulations, and safety certification requirements.
reference: UNECE WP.29 — World Forum for Harmonization of Vehicle Regulations; NHTSA; Euro NCAP

description: SAP S/4HANA material master number (MM module) corresponding to this production variant's configurable material (KMAT). Used for MRP (Material Requirements Planning), production order creation in SAP PP, and cost object controlling in SAP CO.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Material Master; SAP PP — Configurable Materials (KMAT); IATF 16949

description: Date on which this production variant is authorized to enter volume production (SOP — Start of Production). Used for production planning gate reviews, PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) milestone tracking, and supplier readiness confirmation.
reference: APQP (Advanced Product Quality Planning) Phase 4 — Product and Process Validation; IATF 16949

description: Standard labor hours required to complete the full assembly of this production variant from stamping through final assembly and PDI (Pre-Delivery Inspection). Used for production cost standard setting, workforce planning, and SAP CO (Controlling) cost object calculation.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.1; SAP CO Standard Cost Estimation

description: Allocated takt time in seconds for building this production variant on the assigned production line. Represents the available production time divided by customer demand rate. Used for JIS (Just-in-Sequence) scheduling, capacity planning, and bottleneck identification in MES (Manufacturing Execution System).
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.5.1 — Control of Production; SAE J4000 — Lean Manufacturing

description: Cross-reference identifier for this production variant in Siemens Teamcenter PLM (Product Lifecycle Management) variant configuration module. Enables traceability between the manufacturing master data record and the engineering variant definition in the PLM system of record.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM — Variant Configuration; IATF 16949 Clause 7.5 — Documented Information

description: Type of transmission fitted in this production variant: AUTOMATIC (conventional automatic), MANUAL (manual gearbox), CVT (Continuously Variable Transmission), DCT (Dual-Clutch Transmission), or SINGLE_SPEED (for BEV/FCEV). Drives assembly routing to the correct powertrain marriage station and torque tooling specification.
reference: SAE J1297 — Automatic Transmission Functions; IATF 16949 Clause 8.5

description: Alphanumeric code identifying the equipment and feature trim level for this variant (e.g., 'BASE', 'XLE', 'PLATINUM', 'SPORT'). Determines option package applicability, BOM (Bill of Materials) component selection, and MSRP (Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price) tier in the commercial catalog.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM — Variant Configuration; SAP PP — Configurable Materials

description: Timestamp when this production variant record was most recently modified. Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver Layer pipeline and for engineering change audit trail compliance under IATF 16949 documented information control.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 7.5 — Documented Information; ISO 9001 Clause 7.5

description: Indicates whether this production variant is equipped with V2X (Vehicle-to-Everything) communication hardware (True = V2X capable). Drives telematics module assembly sequencing, spectrum licensing compliance, and connected mobility service activation in Geotab/Bosch IoT platform.
reference: SAE J2945 — V2X Communications; ETSI ITS Standards; FCC 47 CFR Part 95

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this production variant within the manufacturing system. Used as the primary business key in MES (Manufacturing Execution System), PLM (Product Lifecycle Management), and SAP PP (Production Planning) for variant identification and cross-system referencing. Sourced from Siemens Teamcenter PLM variant configuration.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.3 — Design and Development; SAP PP Variant Configuration

description: Human-readable descriptive name of the production variant (e.g., 'F-Series SuperCrew 4x4 BEV Long Range'). Used in build sequence planning, shop floor documentation, and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) scheduling displays.

Current lifecycle status of the production variant within the manufacturing master data: ACTIVE (currently buildable), PLANNED (approved for future SOP), INACTIVE (not currently scheduled), DISCONTINUED (past EOP), ON_HOLD (temporarily suspended pending engineering change or regulatory review). Drives MES build feasibility checks.
reference: IATF 16949 Clause 8.3 — Design and Development; SAP PP Material Status

description: OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) internal model code identifying the vehicle platform or nameplate (e.g., 'F150', 'RAV4', 'MODEL3'). Links the production variant to the vehicle program in PLM (Product Lifecycle Management) and SAP MM (Materials Management).
reference: SAE J1100 — Vehicle Dimensions; Siemens Teamcenter PLM

business_glossary_term: Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) Range (km)
description: Official WLTP (Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure) certified driving range in kilometres for BEV and PHEV variants. Null for ICE and HEV variants. Used for EU regulatory labelling, EPA range certification cross-reference, and consumer-facing range claims.
reference: WLTP Regulation (EU) 2017/1151; EPA 40 CFR Part 600 — Fuel Economy Labelling

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the rework order record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7 - Control of Nonconforming Outputs

description: Reference to the quality defect record in the quality domain that triggered this rework order. Links rework traceability to the originating inspection finding or defect notification.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; SAP QM Defect Record

description: Reference to the workforce employee or technician assigned to perform the rework operation. Links to the workforce domain for skill and certification validation.
reference: SAP HR / SuccessFactors Employee Record; IATF 16949 Section 7.2

description: Reference to the manufacturing plant where the rework operation is being executed. Aligns with SAP Plant (Werk) organizational unit.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Organizational Structure; IATF 16949 Section 4.1

description: Reference to the originating production order from which this rework order was raised. Links the rework event back to the scheduled manufacturing work order in SAP PP or MES.
reference: SAP PP Production Order; IATF 16949 Section 8.5.1

description: Reference to the work center or repair station assigned to execute the rework operation. Corresponds to SAP PP Work Center or MES work station definition.
reference: SAP PP Work Center; Apriso/Dassault MES Work Station

description: Actual date and time when the rework operation was completed and the unit was released for re-inspection or returned to the production line. Recorded by MES upon order closure.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES Time Tracking; SAP PM Order Confirmation

description: Actual labor hours consumed to complete the rework operation, recorded upon order completion in MES or SAP PM. Compared against planned hours for efficiency analysis and cost variance reporting.
reference: SAP PM Actual Costs; Apriso/Dassault MES Time Tracking; IATF 16949 Section 9.1

description: Actual date and time when the rework technician began executing the rework operation, as recorded by MES shop floor data collection or operator confirmation.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES Time Tracking; SAP PM Order Confirmation

description: Code representing the specific assembly stage or station within the production line where the nonconformance was detected (e.g., body framing, paint primer, trim line, chassis marriage). Supports JIS (Just-in-Sequence) traceability.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES Station Configuration; IATF 16949 Section 8.5.2

description: The BOM (Bill of Materials) component or part number of the specific sub-assembly or component requiring rework. References the engineering BOM managed in Siemens Teamcenter or SAP MM.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM BOM Management; SAP MM Material Master; IATF 16949 Section 8.5.1

description: Reference number or identifier of the corrective action (CAR) or 8D problem-solving report raised in response to this rework event. Links the rework order to the formal quality improvement process.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 10.2.1 - Corrective Action; SAP QM Corrective Action; APQP 8D Report

description: Date and time when the rework order record was first created in the source system (MES or SAP QM). Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance purposes.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 7.5 - Documented Information; ISO 9001:2015 Section 7.5

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary cost fields on this rework order (rework_labor_cost, rework_material_cost). Typically the plant's local operating currency (e.g., USD, EUR, MXN).
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP FI Currency Configuration

description: Standardized defect classification code identifying the type of nonconformance that triggered the rework order. Aligns with the plant defect code catalogue maintained in SAP QM or MES quality module.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; SAP QM Defect Code Catalogue

description: Free-text narrative description of the defect or nonconformance identified during in-process quality inspection that initiated this rework order. Captured by the quality inspector or MES operator.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; SAP QM Notification Long Text

description: Standardized code identifying the physical location or zone on the vehicle or sub-assembly where the defect was found (e.g., body zone, paint zone, chassis area). Used for spatial defect analysis and NVH (Noise Vibration Harshness) correlation.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; Euro NCAP Defect Zone Classification

description: Code indicating the method by which the defect was detected prior to rework order creation (e.g., visual inspection, automated gauge check, functional test, quality audit, customer feedback). Supports FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) detection ranking analysis.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.6; FMEA Detection Ranking; SAP QM Inspection Method

description: Date and time when the nonconformance was originally detected during in-process quality inspection, triggering the creation of this rework order. The principal business event timestamp for this transaction.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.6; SAP QM Inspection Lot Creation Date; Apriso MES Quality Event

description: Final disposition decision for the nonconforming unit after rework evaluation. Repaired indicates successful correction; scrapped indicates the unit is unrecoverable; concession (use-as-is) indicates acceptance of the nonconformance with documented deviation; return to supplier applies to purchased components.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7.1 - Disposition of Nonconforming Product; ISO 9001:2015 Section 8.7

description: Code identifying the specific quality inspection checkpoint or gate (e.g., body-in-white audit, paint final audit, end-of-line check) at which the defect was detected and the rework order was initiated.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.6; SAP QM Inspection Lot; Apriso MES Quality Gate

description: Indicates whether the vehicle or sub-assembly is placed on a regulatory hold pending rework completion and re-inspection. A regulatory hold prevents the unit from advancing to the next production stage or shipping.
reference: NHTSA 49 CFR Part 573; CARB Compliance; DOT FMVSS; IATF 16949 Section 8.7

description: Indicates whether the defect triggering this rework order is classified as safety-critical, requiring escalation per NHTSA, DOT, or internal safety reporting protocols. Safety-related rework orders may trigger FMEA review and potential field action assessment.
reference: NHTSA 49 CFR Part 573 - Defect and Noncompliance Reports; DOT FMVSS; IATF 16949 Section 9.1.3

description: Indicates whether this rework event caused a production line stoppage (Andon pull or line stop). Used for OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) impact analysis and production downtime reporting.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.5.1; Apriso/Dassault MES Andon Event; SAP PP Downtime Recording

description: The vehicle model year (MY) of the unit undergoing rework. Used for regulatory compliance reporting, warranty analysis, and production quality trending by model year.
reference: NHTSA 49 CFR Part 565; SAP PP Production Version

description: Scheduled date and time when the rework operation is planned to be completed. Used to calculate planned rework cycle time and assess impact on downstream production sequencing.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES Scheduling; SAP PP Scheduling

description: Estimated labor hours planned to complete the rework operation, as defined in the rework routing or standard repair time (SRT) catalogue. Used for capacity planning and cost estimation.
reference: SAP PP Routing Standard Values; IATF 16949 Section 8.5.1

description: Scheduled date and time when the rework operation is planned to begin, as determined by the MES scheduler or production planner. Used for shop floor capacity planning and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) scheduling.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES Scheduling; SAP PP Scheduling

description: Business priority assigned to the rework order to drive scheduling and resource allocation on the shop floor. Critical priority typically indicates a safety-related or regulatory nonconformance requiring immediate resolution.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; SAP QM Notification Priority

description: Code identifying the specific production line (e.g., stamping, body shop, paint, final assembly) where the defect was originally detected and the rework order was raised.
reference: Apriso/Dassault MES Production Line Configuration; SAP PP Work Center Hierarchy

description: Indicates whether a formal re-inspection is required after rework completion before the unit can be released to the next production stage or shipped. Mandatory for safety-related or regulatory nonconformances.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7.1; SAP QM Re-Inspection Trigger

description: Outcome of the quality re-inspection performed after rework completion. Pass indicates the unit meets specification; fail triggers a secondary rework or scrap decision; conditional pass indicates acceptance with documented deviation.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.6; SAP QM Usage Decision; Apriso MES Quality Gate Result

description: Number of rework attempts made on this unit or component for the same defect. Multiple rework attempts on the same unit indicate a chronic quality issue and may trigger escalation or scrap decision per quality policy.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7.1; SAP QM Notification Recurrence

description: Document number or reference to the approved rework instruction, repair standard, or Technical Service Bulletin (TSB) that governs the rework procedure. Ensures traceability to authorized repair methods.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.5.1; SAP DMS Document Reference; Siemens Teamcenter Document Management

description: Total internal labor cost incurred for the rework operation, calculated from actual rework hours and the applicable labor rate. Expressed in the plant's operating currency. Used for quality cost (Cost of Poor Quality - COPQ) reporting.
reference: SAP CO Cost Object Controlling; IATF 16949 Section 9.1; APQP Cost of Poor Quality

description: Cost of replacement parts and materials consumed during the rework operation. Sourced from SAP MM goods issue postings against the rework order. Contributes to total Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) calculation.
reference: SAP MM Goods Issue; SAP CO Cost Object; IATF 16949 Section 9.1

description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the rework order, typically generated by the MES (Manufacturing Execution System) or SAP QM module. Format: RWK-{PlantCode}-{Year}-{Sequence}.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; SAP QM Notification Number

description: Current lifecycle status of the rework order within the shop floor execution workflow. Tracks progression from creation through completion or cancellation as managed in MES or SAP QM.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; Apriso/Dassault MES Order Status

description: Classification of the rework operation method. Inline repair is performed on the moving assembly line; offline rework removes the unit from the line; teardown involves partial or full disassembly; subassembly rework targets a component before vehicle integration; cosmetic repair addresses surface or finish defects. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: inline_repair|offline_rework|teardown|subassembly_rework|cosmetic_repair|field_return_rework — promote to reference product]
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7.1; APQP Phase 4 - Product and Process Validation

description: Standardized code classifying the root cause of the defect as determined through root cause analysis (e.g., 5-Why, Ishikawa). Populated upon rework completion. Supports FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) and SPC (Statistical Process Control) improvement actions.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 10.2; FMEA Methodology; SAP QM Cause Code

description: Number of components or sub-assemblies scrapped as a result of this rework order where repair was not feasible. Used for PPM (Parts Per Million) defect rate calculation and scrap cost reporting.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 8.7; SAP PP Scrap Posting; PPM Defect Rate Reporting

description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this rework order record was sourced (e.g., SAP QM, Apriso/Dassault MES, or manual entry). Supports data lineage and Silver Layer ingestion traceability.
reference: Enterprise Data Governance - Data Lineage Standard; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Conventions

description: Date and time when the rework order record was last modified in the source system. Supports incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver Layer and audit trail requirements.
reference: IATF 16949 Section 7.5 - Documented Information; ISO 9001:2015 Section 7.5

description: Internal product/model code identifying the vehicle nameplate or platform (e.g., truck, SUV, EV, HEV) associated with the rework order. Aligns with PLM product structure in Siemens Teamcenter.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM Product Structure; SAP MM Material Master

description: 17-character Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) of the vehicle or vehicle body on which rework is being performed. Nullable for sub-assembly rework not yet associated with a VIN. Conforms to ISO 3779 standard.
reference: ISO 3779 - Vehicle Identification Number; NHTSA 49 CFR Part 565

Method by which rebate is settled: credit_memo (issued against future purchases), direct_payment (bank transfer or check), offset_against_invoice (deducted from current receivables).

Powertrain types eligible for the rebate: all (any powertrain), ICE (Internal Combustion Engine), HEV (Hybrid Electric Vehicle), PHEV (Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle), EV (Electric Vehicle). Used to target electrification incentives.
Fixed rebate amount paid per vehicle unit sold. Used for flat-rate rebate structures. Null if percentage-based rebate is used.
Percentage rate applied to eligible transaction amounts to calculate rebate accrual. Used for percentage-based rebate structures. Null if fixed amount rebate is used.
Geographic sales region or territory to which this rebate agreement applies. Used for regional incentive programs and performance tracking.
SAP SD rebate agreement reference number from transaction codes BO01 (create) or BO02 (change). Used for system integration and traceability.
Frequency at which accrued rebates are paid out to the beneficiary: monthly, quarterly, semi_annual, annual, or upon_completion (at agreement end).

Current status of rebate settlement: not_started (no payments made), in_progress (settlement cycle active), partially_settled (some payments made), fully_settled (all accruals paid), disputed (settlement under review).
Target number of vehicle units that must be sold or delivered to qualify for the rebate. Null for non-volume-based agreements.
Explanation for why the rebate agreement was terminated early, if applicable. Null for agreements that expired naturally or are still active.
Cumulative rebate amount accrued under this agreement as of the last calculation date. Represents the liability owed to the beneficiary.
Cumulative rebate amount paid out to the beneficiary through credit memos or direct payments. Used to track settlement progress.

Comma-separated list of vehicle models or model families eligible for this rebate agreement. May reference SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) codes or model year (MY) designations. Empty indicates all models are eligible.
Unique identifier for the bad debt write-off record. Primary key.
Reference to the billing account from which the receivable is being written off.
Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Cost‑center linkage for write‑offs supports expense analysis of bad‑debt.
Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Write‑off entries must be posted to a GL account; replaces denormalized code.
Reference to the primary invoice associated with this write-off. Links to the original billing document.
Reference to the dealership if the write-off relates to dealer invoicing or dealer-originated receivables. Nullable for direct retail transactions.
Reference to the employee or manager who authorized the write-off. Links to workforce/employee master data.
Reference to the retail customer or fleet account associated with the written-off receivable. Links to customer master data.
Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Profit‑center association for write‑offs enables profitability impact assessment.
Foreign key linking to vehicle.vin_registry. Business justification: Write‑offs of vehicle invoices must be tied to the underlying vehicle for loss analysis and compliance reporting.
Reference to the employee or manager who authorized the write-off. Links to workforce/employee master data.
Reference to the retail customer or fleet account associated with the written-off receivable. Links to customer master data.
Reference to the dealership if the write-off relates to dealer invoicing or dealer-originated receivables. Nullable for direct retail transactions.
The total monetary value of the receivable being written off. Represents the net uncollectable balance.
Full name of the individual who approved the write-off, captured for audit trail purposes.
The date on which the write-off was formally approved by the authorized authority.
The organizational level at which the write-off was approved, typically based on write-off amount thresholds. Values: manager, director, vp (vice president), cfo (chief financial officer).
The business unit or division responsible for the original sale (e.g., vehicle sales, parts, service). Used for divisional bad debt reporting.
Reference to the third-party collection agency assigned to pursue recovery of the written-off debt. Nullable if no agency was engaged.

Current status of collection efforts for the written-off debt. Values: not_assigned (no collection action), assigned (sent to agency), in_progress (active collection), recovered (payment received), closed (collection efforts ceased).
The user ID or username of the system user who created the write-off record. Used for audit trail and accountability.
The system timestamp when the write-off record was first created in the database. Used for audit trail and data lineage.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the write-off amount (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY).
The number of days the receivable was overdue at the time of write-off. Used for aging analysis and credit policy evaluation.
The fiscal period (month or quarter) within the fiscal year when the write-off was recorded.
The fiscal year in which the write-off was recorded, used for financial reporting and period analysis.
Reference number for any associated legal case, bankruptcy filing, or court proceeding related to the write-off. Nullable if no legal action was involved.
Free-text field for additional comments, supporting documentation references, or special circumstances related to the write-off decision.
The original payment due date of the invoice before it became delinquent and was subsequently written off.
The original gross amount of the invoice before any payments, credits, or write-offs were applied. Provides context for the write-off magnitude.
The receivable balance that was outstanding immediately before the write-off was applied. May differ from original invoice amount if partial payments were received.
The accounting period date when the write-off was posted to the general ledger. May differ from write_off_date for period-end adjustments.

Standardized code indicating the primary reason for the write-off. Values: bankruptcy (customer filed for bankruptcy), insolvency (customer insolvent), uncontactable (customer cannot be reached), statute_of_limitations (debt legally uncollectable), commercial_settlement (negotiated settlement), fraud (fraudulent transaction).
reference: Internal Credit Risk Policy, GAAP Bad Debt Guidelines

description: Detailed narrative explanation of the circumstances leading to the write-off decision. Provides additional context beyond the reason code.
The monetary amount recovered after the write-off was recorded. Null if no recovery has occurred. Used to track bad debt recovery income.
The date on which a recovery payment was received for a previously written-off receivable. Null if no recovery has occurred.
Boolean indicator of whether any portion of the written-off amount was subsequently recovered. True if recovery occurred, False otherwise.
The sales region or geographic territory associated with the original sale. Used for regional bad debt analysis.
The SAP accounting document number for the general ledger posting of the write-off. May differ from the write-off document number in multi-step posting scenarios.
The SAP FI document number generated when the write-off was posted to the financial system. Used for reconciliation and audit trail.
The user ID or username of the system user who last modified the write-off record. Used for audit trail and accountability.
The system timestamp when the write-off record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.
Indicates whether the write-off is for the full outstanding balance or a partial amount. Values: full (entire balance written off), partial (portion of balance written off).
The date on which the formal decision to write off the uncollectable receivable was executed. This is the business event date for the write-off.
reference: GAAP Revenue Recognition ASC 606, IFRS 9 Financial Instruments

description: Business-readable unique identifier for the write-off transaction, typically following organizational numbering convention (e.g., WO-20240001234).
Unique identifier for the price condition record. Primary key.
add column jurisdiction_id (BIGINT) with FK to compliance.jurisdiction.jurisdiction_id - pricing conditions vary by tax/regulatory jurisdiction
Indicates whether application of this pricing condition requires managerial or pricing authority approval before being applied to a billing transaction. True requires approval workflow.
User ID or name of the pricing authority or manager who approved this condition for use in billing transactions. Null if approval is not required or pending.
Date and time when this pricing condition was approved for use. Null if approval is not required or still pending. Part of the governance audit trail.

Method used to calculate the condition value in the billing transaction. Defines whether the condition is applied as a fixed amount, percentage of base, quantity-dependent, or using a tiered/formula approach.
High-level classification of the condition type grouping similar pricing elements together for reporting and analysis purposes.
Detailed textual description of the pricing condition, including its business purpose, applicability rules, and any special terms or restrictions. Provides context for pricing analysts and auditors.
Indicates whether this condition is marked for exclusion from certain pricing scenarios or customer groups. True means the condition should be excluded under specific business rules.
Business identifier for the pricing condition record, typically sourced from SAP SD condition record (KONP table). Used for external reference and traceability.
Current lifecycle status of the pricing condition record. Active conditions are available for use in billing; inactive, expired, or suspended conditions are not applied.
Sequence number within the pricing procedure that defines the order in which this condition is evaluated and applied during billing calculation.

Type of pricing condition applied to the billing transaction. Defines whether this is a base price (MSRP), negotiated price, discount, surcharge, tax, or other pricing element. Aligns with SAP SD condition types. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: msrp|negotiated|fleet_discount|dealer_margin|volume_rebate|freight|pdi_charge|tax|surcharge|promotional_discount — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Unit of measure for the condition value. Indicates whether the value is an absolute amount, a percentage, or a per-unit rate.

Monetary or percentage value of the pricing condition. For absolute amounts, represents the price or adjustment in the condition currency. For percentage-based conditions, represents the rate (e.g., 5.5 for 5.5%).
Date and time when this pricing condition record was first created in the system. Part of the audit trail for master data lifecycle tracking.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the condition value when expressed as an absolute amount (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY).
Type of customer for which this pricing condition is applicable. Enables customer segment-specific pricing strategies (retail, fleet, dealer, government, commercial).

Unique identifier of the dealer or dealership for which this pricing condition is applicable. Enables dealer-specific pricing agreements and margin structures. Null indicates condition applies to all dealers.
SAP SD distribution channel code indicating the sales channel (e.g., retail, fleet, online) for which this condition applies. Enables channel-specific pricing strategies.
Precise date and time when this pricing condition record version is superseded or becomes inactive in the lakehouse. Null indicates the current active version. Used for SCD Type 2 tracking.
Precise date and time when this pricing condition record becomes effective in the lakehouse. Used for temporal queries and slowly changing dimension (SCD) Type 2 tracking.
Indicates whether this record represents the current active version of the pricing condition. True for the latest version, False for historical versions. Supports SCD Type 2 queries.
User ID or name of the person who last modified this pricing condition record. Supports change tracking and accountability.
Date and time when this pricing condition record was last modified. Enables change detection and version control for pricing master data.

Indicates whether sales or billing personnel are permitted to manually override this condition value during transaction processing. True allows manual adjustment, False enforces system-determined value.
Model year of the vehicle for which this pricing condition is applicable. Enables year-over-year pricing adjustments and end-of-model-year promotions.
Reference to the SAP SD pricing procedure that governs the sequence and logic of condition application. Links this condition to the broader pricing determination framework.
SAP SD sales organization code that owns this pricing condition. Defines the organizational unit responsible for pricing governance and approval.

Geographic sales region or market code for which this pricing condition is valid. Enables region-specific pricing strategies to account for market conditions, competition, and regulatory requirements.
Name of the SAP SD condition table (e.g., A001, A002) from which this condition record is sourced. Provides traceability to the source system configuration.
Reference to the SAP SD KONP table record number that stores the condition record master data. Enables direct linkage to the source system for audit and reconciliation.
Reference to the SAP SD KONV table counter that tracks condition application instances in sales and billing documents. Used for transaction-level traceability.
Basis for scale-based pricing conditions. Defines the dimension (quantity, value, weight, volume) used to determine tiered pricing or volume-based discounts.
Lower bound of the scale range for tiered pricing conditions. Defines the minimum quantity or value at which this condition rate applies.
Upper bound of the scale range for tiered pricing conditions. Defines the maximum quantity or value at which this condition rate applies. Null indicates no upper limit.
Identifier of the source system from which this pricing condition record was extracted (e.g., SAP_SD, SFDC, DMS). Supports multi-system integration and data lineage tracking.
Start date from which this pricing condition becomes effective and can be applied to billing transactions. Part of the condition validity period.
End date until which this pricing condition remains effective. Null indicates the condition is valid indefinitely. Part of the condition validity period.
Code identifying the specific vehicle model to which this pricing condition applies. Enables model-specific pricing and promotional strategies. Null indicates condition applies across all models.
Trim or configuration level of the vehicle model for which this condition applies (e.g., base, sport, luxury, premium). Enables trim-specific pricing differentiation.
User ID or name of the person who created this pricing condition record in the system. Supports audit trail and accountability.
Unique identifier for the dunning record. Primary key.
Reference to the billing account that is subject to dunning activity due to overdue receivables.
Reference to the collections specialist or team responsible for managing this dunning case and follow-up actions.
Reference to the collections specialist or team responsible for managing this dunning case and follow-up actions.

The classification of the billing account subject to dunning. Dealer accounts are franchise dealerships, fleet accounts are corporate fleet customers, retail accounts are individual consumers, commercial accounts are business customers, government accounts are public sector entities.
The date and time when this dunning record was first created in the system.
The total outstanding receivables for the account at the time of the dunning run, including both overdue and current amounts. Confidential business data.
The approved credit limit for the billing account at the time of the dunning run. Confidential business data.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the overdue amount (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY).
The business segment or risk classification of the customer, influencing dunning strategy and escalation path.
The number of days between the oldest overdue date and the dunning run date, representing the age of the oldest delinquency.
The email address, postal address, or portal user ID to which the dunning notice was sent. Confidential organizational contact data.
Indicates whether the customer has raised a dispute regarding the overdue charges (True) or not (False).
Free-text description of the reason provided by the customer for disputing the overdue charges.
The date on which the dunning block was applied to the account. Null if not blocked.
Indicates whether further dunning activity for this account has been temporarily blocked (True) due to dispute, payment arrangement, or other reason, or is active (False).
The reason why dunning activity has been blocked for this account. Null if not blocked.
The administrative fee charged to the customer for this dunning notice, if applicable. Zero if no fee charged.
The escalation level of the dunning notice. Level 1 is initial reminder, Level 2 is warning, Level 3 is final demand, Legal indicates legal action initiated.
The channel through which the dunning notice was delivered to the customer.
The date and time when the dunning notice was successfully transmitted to the customer.

The type of dunning communication sent to the customer. Reminder is courtesy notice, warning indicates escalation, final demand is last notice before legal action, legal notice indicates attorney involvement, suspension notice warns of service suspension, account hold indicates credit freeze.
The date on which the dunning run was executed and this dunning notice was generated.
Business identifier for the dunning run batch that generated this notice. Format: DUN-YYYYMMDD-NNNN.

The current lifecycle status of this dunning record. Sent indicates notice generated, delivered indicates successful transmission, bounced indicates delivery failure, responded indicates customer reply received, escalated indicates moved to higher level, resolved indicates payment received or dispute settled, cancelled indicates dunning withdrawn. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sent|delivered|bounced|responded|escalated|resolved|cancelled — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The late payment interest accrued on the overdue amount as of the dunning run date, if applicable. Zero if no interest charged.
The date and time when this dunning record was last updated.
The scheduled date for the next follow-up action or escalation if payment is not received.
The type of follow-up action planned for the next action date.
Free-text notes and comments from collections staff regarding this dunning case, customer interactions, and follow-up actions.
The due date of the oldest unpaid invoice included in this dunning action, indicating how long the account has been delinquent.
The number of individual overdue invoices or line items included in this dunning notice.
The amount the customer has committed to pay by the promise date. May be partial or full overdue amount.
The date by which the customer has promised to remit payment, if a payment promise was received. Null otherwise.
The date on which the dunning case was resolved through payment, dispute settlement, or write-off. Null if still open.
The manner in which the dunning case was resolved. Null if still open.
The date on which the customer responded to the dunning notice. Null if no response received.
Indicates whether the customer has responded to this dunning notice (True) or not (False).

The nature of the customer response to the dunning notice. Payment promise indicates commitment to pay, dispute raised indicates disagreement with charges, payment plan request indicates request for installment arrangement, contact request indicates need for discussion.
The SAP FI dunning document number generated by the dunning program. 10-digit numeric identifier.
The total amount of receivables that are overdue and subject to this dunning action, in the billing currency.
Unique identifier for the payment term record. Primary key.
Foreign key linking to billing.account. Business justification: Accounts often have a default payment term; linking provides a normalized reference.
Comma-separated list of billing account types to which this payment term applies (e.g., dealer, fleet, retail, corporate, OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer)).
Date on which this payment term was approved by finance or credit management. Null if not yet approved.
Indicates whether finance or credit manager approval is required before this payment term can be assigned to a customer account.
Name or user ID of the finance or credit manager who approved this payment term for use. Null if no approval required or pending.
Indicates whether automatic dunning (collection reminder) process is enabled for invoices using this payment term.
Rule defining the baseline date from which net due days and discount days are calculated (invoice date, delivery date, end of month, or custom).
Code identifying the business unit or division that owns and manages this payment term (e.g., DEALER, FLEET, PARTS).
Date and time when this payment term record was first created in the system.
Indicates whether a credit check is required before this payment term can be assigned to a billing account.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for which this payment term is defined (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY). Null if applicable to all currencies.
Number of days from invoice date within which discount percentage 1 applies.
Number of days from invoice date within which discount percentage 2 applies (typically longer than discount days 1).
First early payment discount percentage offered if payment is made within discount days 1 (e.g., 2.00 for 2%).
Second early payment discount percentage offered if payment is made within discount days 2 (typically lower than discount 1).
Default dunning level (escalation stage) for collection reminders associated with this payment term. Null if auto dunning is disabled.
Date after which this payment term is no longer valid for new assignments. Null if no end date is defined.
Date from which this payment term becomes valid and available for assignment to billing accounts.
If baseline date rule is custom, specifies a fixed day of the month for payment due date (e.g., 15 for the 15th of each month). Null if not applicable.
User ID or name of the person who last modified this payment term record.
Date and time when this payment term record was last updated.
Maximum invoice or order value for which this payment term is applicable. Null if no maximum.
Minimum invoice or order value required for this payment term to be applicable. Null if no minimum.
Number of days from invoice date by which full payment is due without penalty.
Free-text field for additional notes, special conditions, or internal comments about this payment term.
Comma-separated list of allowed payment methods for this term (e.g., wire_transfer, check, ACH, credit_card). Empty if no restriction.
Short alphanumeric code representing the payment term (e.g., NET30, 2/10N30, COD). Maps to SAP FI payment term key in table T052.
Detailed explanation of the payment term conditions, including discount and penalty clauses.
Full descriptive name of the payment term (e.g., Net 30 Days, 2% 10 Net 30, Cash on Delivery).
Current lifecycle status of the payment term: active (in use), inactive (not available for new assignments), deprecated (legacy term), or pending approval (awaiting finance approval).
Method used to calculate late payment penalties: daily accrual, monthly accrual, flat fee, or none.
Number of days after net due date before penalty charges begin to accrue.
Late payment penalty rate applied after grace period expires, expressed as percentage per period (e.g., 1.5% per month).
Three-letter geographic region code where this payment term is applicable (e.g., USA, EUR, JPN). Null if globally applicable.
